posts.title: The Quiet Demise of the Leap Second
posts.description: In October 2026, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures decided to abolish leap seconds, which were additional seconds added at the end of June or December This change will allow UTC to gradually drift from mean solar time, potentially requiring a leap hour in thousands of years. The final leap second occurred on December 31, 2016.… Continue reading The Quiet Demise of the Leap Second →

posts.title: Solar Time vs Time Zones: Europe’s Clock Mismatch
posts.description: The article examines the discrepancies between local time and solar time in Europe, noting that many EU countries, despite diverse longitudes, share the same time zone. It discusses types of time, the historical shifts in timekeeping, the debates on restoring natural time as civil time… Continue reading Solar Time vs Time Zones: Europe’s Clock Mismatch →

posts.title: Daylight Saving Time: History, Benefits, Pitfalls and Decline
posts.description: At 2 AM local time on Sunday 25 October, the UK like most of Europe will put it clocks back by one hour as Daylight Saving Time (DST) ends. Most of the USA will follow a week later.
